paragraphs.text: Wellington R1461 of 15 Operational Training Unit took off from RAF Harwell on a night navigation exercise and crashed at Llansilin on 26 January 1943; the inscription gives the time as 0146 hrs. IBCC says the aircraft was seen on fire before it struck a hillside and then a farmhouse. The Air of Authority casualty listing says it crashed in flames, possibly after hitting high ground. The two civilians in the farmhouse, Edwin Williams and his wife Annie Jane, died with the crew. Sources disagree on the serial: the plaque and IWM give R1461, while IBCC and Air of Authority give R1491.

Five sergeants of the RAFVR died. IBCC lists John Simpson Todd (22) as wireless operator and Cadfan Edwards (24) as WOp/AG. Air of Authority gives Geoffrey George Ottley (20), Leonard Charles Muston (28) and Brace Harry Parker (26); we found no source for their crew roles. Todd and Muston are buried at Oswestry General Cemetery. Edwards, Ottley and Parker are commemorated on the Runnymede Memorial.

IWM records a wall-mounted tablet of Welsh slate, in good condition, at Bwlch Y Rhiw Farmhouse on the B4580, Llansilin. It is on the house, which is the crash site. IWM does not state who made or erected it, when it was dedicated or who looks after it, and we found no other source that does. IBCC calls the county Montgomeryshire; IWM gives Glyndwr, Clwyd.

notes: DIED_COUNT: our died_count 2 and names_on_memorial 2 match IWM's civilian count (Edwin and Annie Jane Williams); IWM lists 5 service dead separately and its 'names listed' section is empty. The inscription names 7 people. The five airmen are the whole crew per the plaque ('entire crew'). Dossier claims died_count 5 (airmen only); a human should decide whether the record's field means airmen or all dead. SERIAL CONFLICT: plaque/IWM R1461 vs IBCC (Todd, Edwards), Air of Authority R1491; ASN and baaa-acro (search snippets) also gave R1491 but were not read in full (ASN wikibase 152182 returned 403; linked from IWM). Left unresolved. ROLES: our record has Ottley pilot, Muston navigator, Todd bomb aimer, Edwards and Parker 'Crew'. IBCC says Todd wireless operator and Edwards WOp/AG, which contradicts 'Bomb Aimer' for Todd; Ottley/Muston/Parker roles unsourced, so left as gaps (crew roles cannot be retracted by dossier). NATIONALITY: record says British; only Todd/Edwards have a source (IBCC country of origin United Kingdom); others unsourced. COUNTY: record says Clwyd (IWM); IBCC says Montgomeryshire, Hansard Denbighshire, user brief says now Powys; no county claim made. CUSTODIAN: the tablet is on a private farmhouse; no source names a maker, erector, dedication date or custodian; status 'unknown' not 'unknown-confirmed' because Shropshire Star, Traces of War (403), Oswestry genealogy page (domain expired) and ASN could not be read. Leads: Shropshire Star article (fetch blocked; read via search summary only), Traces of War sights/118488, Oswestry Family & Local History Group, Llansilin community council, Oswestry RBL. CWGC pages for Ottley, Edwards, Todd, Parker and IBCC pages for Ottley, Muston, Parker were not found. PHOTOS: IWM main image credited Huw Davies, but which of the two stored media.iwm.org.uk URLs is his was not verified, so none included. A 'McKoy, Godfrey Alan RNZAF' entry on the same date in Air of Authority is an unrelated Spitfire loss (64 Sqn), not this crew. A direct curl of rafweb was declined by the harness, so only WebFetch was used.
